subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "Bread and butter ______ his favorite breakfast."
explanation: When two nouns express a single compound idea or dish, singular verb "is" is used.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "Either the teacher or the students ______ responsible."
explanation: With "either...or", the verb agrees with the nearer plural subject ("students").

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "The quality of these mangoes ______ not good."
explanation: The subject is singular "quality", not plural "mangoes".

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "Neither of the candidates ______ qualified."
explanation: Distributive pronoun "Neither" takes a singular verb.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "The jury ______ divided in their opinions."
explanation: When members of a collective noun act individually or disagree, plural verb "were" is used.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "Physics ______ an interesting branch of science."
explanation: Subject names ending in -s are grammatically singular.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "The news ______ true."
explanation: "News" is uncountable and singular.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "The captain along with his team members ______ arriving today."
explanation: Parenthetical phrases like "along with" do not affect the main singular subject "captain".

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "Fifty thousand rupees ______ a large amount."
explanation: A sum of money regarded as a singular whole takes a singular verb.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "Many a student ______ failed in the test."
explanation: "Many a + singular noun" is followed by a singular verb ("has").

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "A number of students ______ waiting outside."
explanation: "A number of" takes a plural verb, whereas "The number of" takes singular.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "The number of applicants ______ fifty."
explanation: "The number of" takes a singular verb.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "Every boy and every girl ______ given a prize."
explanation: Nouns qualified by "every" connected by "and" require a singular verb.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "No news ______ good news."
explanation: "News" governs singular verb "is".

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "Gulliver's Travels ______ written by Jonathan Swift."
explanation: Titles of single books take a singular verb.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "Neither you nor I ______ to blame."
explanation: With "neither...nor", verb agrees in person with the closer subject ("I am").

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "Two-thirds of the city ______ destroyed by fire."
explanation: Fractions of an uncountable/singular noun ("city") take a singular verb.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "Two-thirds of the books ______ sold."
explanation: Fractions of a plural countable noun ("books") take a plural verb.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "The Arabian Nights ______ still a popular book."
explanation: Title of a literary collection takes a singular verb.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "Time and tide ______ for no man."
explanation: Traditional plural agreement for "Time and tide".

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "More than one person ______ involved in the fraud."
explanation: "More than one + singular noun" takes a singular verb.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "Slow and steady ______ the race."
explanation: Compound singular subject expressing a single concept takes singular verb "wins".

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "The Prime Minister as well as his cabinet ministers ______ present."
explanation: "As well as" does not alter the singular subject "Prime Minister".

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "The cattle ______ grazing in the meadow."
explanation: "Cattle" is inherently plural.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "The scissors ______ very sharp."
explanation: Two-part instruments (scissors, tongs, spectacles) take plural verbs.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "A pair of scissors ______ kept on the desk."
explanation: "A pair of" is singular and takes a singular verb.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "Measles ______ an infectious disease."
explanation: Disease names ending in -s (measles, mumps) take singular verbs.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "Not only Ali but also his brothers ______ invited."
explanation: Verb agrees with the closer subject "brothers" (plural).

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "Everybody ______ done his duty."
explanation: Indefinite pronoun "Everybody" takes singular verb "has".

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "All that glitters ______ not gold."
explanation: Standard proverb uses singular verb "is".

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "Ten kilometers ______ not a long walk for an athlete."
explanation: Distance as a single measure takes a singular verb.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "The United States ______ a powerful nation."
explanation: Country names take singular verbs.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "One of my friends ______ living in Canada."
explanation: Singular subject "One" governs "is".

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "None of the money ______ recovered."
explanation: "Money" is uncountable, so "none" takes singular verb "was".

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "Politics ______ a complicated field."
explanation: "Politics" takes a singular verb when referring to the field/discipline.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "The police ______ investigating the case."
explanation: "Police" is a collective plural noun.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "The majority of students ______ passed."
explanation: "Majority of + plural noun" takes a plural verb.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "A bouquet of yellow roses ______ presented to the guest."
explanation: Subject is singular "bouquet".

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "There ______ many reasons for his absence."
explanation: With dummy "There", verb agrees with following plural subject "many reasons".

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: "Neither of the two roads ______ to the railway station."
explanation: "Neither" takes a singular verb ("leads").

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: Choose the correct verb: "The jury ________ divided in their individual opinions."
explanation: When members of a collective noun act individually or have differing opinions ("their opinions"), a plural verb ("were") is used.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: Select the correct sentence:

options.A: Bread and butter is a staple breakfast in many households.
options.B: Bread and butter are a staple breakfast in many households.
options.C: Bread and butter were a staple breakfast in many households.
options.D: Bread and butter have been a staple breakfast in many households.

explanation: When two nouns express a single compound idea or unit (bread and butter as a dish), the verb is singular ("is").

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: Choose the correct verb: "The commander, along with his brave soldiers, ________ awarded medals."
explanation: Intervening parenthetical phrases introduced by "along with" do not change the number of the subject ("commander" is singular -> "was").

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: Fill in the blank: "Every one of the participants ________ given a participation certificate."
explanation: "Every one" is an indefinite singular pronoun requiring a singular verb ("was").

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: Select the grammatically correct option: "Neither the teacher nor the students ________ present in the auditorium."
explanation: With "neither...nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject ("students" is plural -> "were").

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: Choose the correct verb: "A number of qualified candidates ________ applied for the internship."
explanation: "A number of" takes a plural verb ("have applied"), whereas "The number of" takes a singular verb.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: Fill in the blank: "The news broadcast by the national media ________ verified by official sources."
explanation: "News" is singular in construction and takes a singular verb ("was").

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: Select the correct form: "Mathematics ________ considered a compulsory subject in secondary school."
explanation: Names of subjects/disciplines ending in -s (Mathematics, Physics, Civics) take a singular verb.

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: Fill in the blank: "Fifty thousand rupees ________ a reasonable sum for this repair work."
explanation: A specific amount of money thought of as a single total quantity takes a singular verb ("is").

subject: English
topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
question: Choose the correct verb: "More than one candidate ________ selected for the scholarship."
explanation: "More than one" is followed by a singular noun and takes a singular verb ("was").
